title: Senior Data Center Operations Engineer
description:
We are looking for an experienced Data Center Operations Engineer to join our growing team in Milan and help shape the future of our flagship project, Colosseum, one of Europe’s most powerful AI supercomputers, currently in development.

Designed to run our proprietary AI models at scale, it forms the compute backbone behind the intelligence we deliver to the world’s most demanding industries.

To achieve the highest level of performance, datacenter infrastructure has become a tightly integrated part of supercomputers where power, cooling and the building management systems provide critical consumable resources that should be optimized like any other resource in the system to extract maximum performance in a reliable way. We also strive towards optimal responsible embedding in the local environment. Tuning the heat recovery systems to optimize for the community district heating systems and tuning the power systems to support and stabilize the local grid are critically important to deliver on our societal responsibilities.

In this role, you will maintain the infrastructure and ensure its reliability and performance. You will respond to incidents and support troubleshooting and resolution activities when issues arise.

You will also contribute to the architecture and design of next-generation systems, helping shape future infrastructure evolution. A key part of the role involves automating processes, integrating systems, and implementing ongoing improvements and optimizations.

As a part of the team, you will stay up to date with the latest technologies and industry trends, actively bringing new ideas. You will collaborate closely with other team members to evaluate and implement these improvements effectively.

What You Have

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or Computer Engineering, or a related field.

  • At least 6 years of experience as a Data Center Operations Engineer or in similar roles.

  • Certification to work with MV/LV electrical systems (Medium Voltage / Low Voltage)

  • Certifications (PES / PAV / PEI or equivalent, DCIS or equivalent)

  • Strong understanding of data center operations and critical infrastructure environments

  • Solid knowledge of industry standards, including ISO 50001 (Energy Management Systems)

  • Hands-on experience with data center monitoring, control, and integration systems, including BMC for the IT hardware and related tools

  • Experience with infrastructure monitoring and management protocols such as Redfish, SNMP, and MQTT

  • Working knowledge of Python for automation and integration tasks

  • Experience with modern system integration frameworks and APIs (e.g. MCP or similar technologies)

Who You Are

  • A versatile engineer, comfortable operating in complex and fast-paced environments.

  • Driven and fearless, you proactively tackle challenges and overcome obstacles with determination.

  • A systems thinker, capable of understanding the broader architecture and identifying dependencies across platforms and technologies.

  • A collaborative team player who is enthusiastic, curious, and passionate about problem-solving, thriving both independently and within cross-functional teams.

  • An effective communicator with strong interpersonal skills, able to engage with diverse stakeholders and foster collaboration.

  • Fluent in English and eager to contribute in a multicultural and international environment.

Benefits

Perks

  • Learning Friday. If our team members know more, so do we. That’s why we give everyone a training budget that they can spend on books, online courses or other training materials.

  • Smart Working. Trains can be a drag, you can save some commuting time by working from home.

  • Salary is based on experience and topped up with other bonuses.

We offer a competitive salary, as well as an opportunity to receive company equity. The typical salary for this role ranges between € 50.000 and € 70.000. As you gain experience and make more significant contributions to the business, your compensation will be reviewed to match your impact. Additionally, depending on your seniority and your performance, you’ll have the opportunity to receive stock options, with a variable value calculated from your base salary, giving you the chance to directly participate in the company’s success.

About Domyn

Domyn is a company specializing in the research and development of Responsible AI for regulated industries, including financial services, government, and heavy industry. It supports enterprises with proprietary, fully governable solutions based on a composable AI architecture — including LLMs, AI agents, and one of the world’s largest supercomputers. At the core of Domyn’s product offer is a chip-to-frontend architecture that allows organizations to control the entire AI stack — from hardware to application — ensuring isolation, security, and governance throughout the AI lifecycle. Its foundational LLMs, Domyn Large and Domyn Small, are designed for advanced reasoning and optimized to understand each business’s specific language, logic, and context. Provided under an open-enterprise license, these models can be fully transferred and owned by clients. Once deployed, they enable customizable agents that operate on proprietary data to solve complex, domain-specific problems. All solutions are managed via a unified platform with native tools for access management, traceability, and security. Powering it all, Colosseum — a supercomputer in development using NVIDIA Grace Blackwell Superchips — will train next-gen models exceeding 1T parameters. Domyn partners with Microsoft, NVIDIA, and G42. Clients include Allianz, Intesa Sanpaolo, and Fincantieri.

title: SSC Supervisor
description:
SUMMARY

The SSC Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the day-to-day operations of the Shared Service Centre (SSC) in Poland, ensuring the accurate, timely, and controlled delivery of invoicing and related support services across multiple business locations.

This role combines operational leadership with hands-on process oversight, ensuring that service delivery meets established quality, compliance, and performance standards. The SSC Supervisor will provide direction, coaching, and support to the SSC team while driving accountability, efficiency, and continuous improvement.

As the SSC evolves and expands, the role will play a key part in developing scalable processes, strengthening internal controls, establishing best practices, and supporting the successful transition of invoicing activities from additional countries into the SSC. Given the direct impact of invoicing activities on customer satisfaction, revenue recognition, cash flow, and financial performance, maintaining service excellence, timeliness, and operational discipline will be critical to success.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Coordinate and oversee daily SSC operations, ensuring workload is effectively distributed, priorities are clearly defined, and service commitments are consistently achieved.

  • Lead, supervise, coach, and support SSC team members, promoting a culture of accountability, quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

  • Monitor workflow, service levels, and operational performance to ensure activities are completed accurately and within agreed timelines, proactively addressing any delays or bottlenecks.

  • Ensure compliance with established Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), internal controls, company policies, escalation procedures, and reporting requirements.

  • Take ownership of complex operational issues, driving resolution and implementing corrective actions to prevent recurrence and improve overall process effectiveness.

  • Act as the primary operational point of contact for key stakeholders across Finance, Operations, Commercial, and country teams, ensuring effective communication and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Support the onboarding, training, and development of SSC employees, ensuring consistent knowledge transfer and adherence to standardised processes.

  • Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), service quality, operational backlogs, and issue resolution activities, identifying risks and implementing mitigation plans where required.

  • Support the successful implementation and stabilisation of the new Financial Module and other systems impacting SSC operations.

  • Contribute to the establishment and ongoing development of the SSC by designing, documenting, and enhancing processes, controls, and service standards that support sustainable growth and operational excellence.

  • Identify opportunities for process optimisation, automation, and efficiency improvements, supporting the SSC's long-term strategy and continuous improvement objectives.

  • Ensure a strong customer-focused approach to service delivery, maintaining high levels of responsiveness and stakeholder satisfaction.

  • Assist with future transition and migration activities as invoicing processes from additional locations are integrated into the SSC structure.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum 5 years of experience in a Shared Services Centre (SSC), finance operations, commercial operations, business support, or a similar service delivery environment, including experience coordinating processes, managing priorities, and supporting operational performance.

  • Degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred. Equivalent relevant professional experience and demonstrated capability in a comparable role will also be considered.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES

  • Experience coordinating or supervising teams within a transactional, operational, or shared services environment.

  • Strong understanding of Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), internal controls, and escalation processes.

  • Experience working with ERP systems, with strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other reporting and data analysis tools.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English; proficiency in additional European languages would be considered an advantage.

  • Experience supporting Shared Service Centre operations, transitions, or process migrations is preferred. Previous experience within the inspection, oil and gas, logistics, laboratory services, industrial services, or a related industry would be advantageous.

  • Flexible and resilient with a problem-solving attitude.

  • Willingness to participate in training courses as required.

  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office applications.

COMPETENCIES

  • Execution and Service Delivery: Drives timely, accurate completion of SSC activities by setting clear priorities, following through on commitments, and maintaining focus on service quality, deadlines, and issue resolution.

  • Ownership and Accountability: Takes responsibility for team output, service performance, and operational follow-through, ensuring issues are fully understood, addressed, and escalated when needed.

  • Leading and Developing Others: Guides, supports, and motivates team members by setting clear expectations, reinforcing consistent ways of working, and building capability through coaching, feedback, and knowledge transfer.

  • Stakeholder Communication & Collaboration: Works effectively across Operations, Finance, Commercial, and local teams to align priorities, resolve issues, and maintain clear communication with stakeholders.

  • Process Discipline and Continuous Improvement: Strengthens developing SSC processes by applying structured ways of working, supporting controls, identifying improvement opportunities, and helping build scalable service delivery.

  • Performance Management: Uses workload, backlog, quality, KPI, and service performance information to identify risks, support decisions, and drive timely corrective action.

  • Customer and Business Orientation: Understands how service performance affects customer satisfaction, revenue recognition, cash flow reliability, and broader operational outcomes.

  • Change Agility: Supports the transition to a developing SSC model by helping the team adapt to new processes, responsibilities, tools, and service expectations.

title: Line Worker
description:
The starting rate for this position is $17.00, incremental increases are earned through developing skills and qualifications.

Summary

This position is a Processing Line Worker in a Food Processing (Eggs) company. Under the direction of the Processing Supervisor, this position performs various tasks ensuring the highest quality product possible.

Key Responsibilities

  • Food Safety and Food Quality
    • Perform all functions of the position with strict adherence to all HACCP, SQF, cGMP’s, and regulatory protocols.
    • Follows food safety principals.
    • Ensure that products and materials are handled and stored in such a way as to prevent damage or product contamination.
    • Examine product to verify conformance to quality standards.
    • Maintain compliance with the personnel and process hygiene requirements.
  • Operations
    • Grades and aligns eggs entering the washer section.
    • Provides for smooth transition of eggs from main egg belt conveyor to the accumulating station.
    • Keeps area clean, tracks inedible, dumps inedible into auger.
    • Cleans washer screens.
    • Performs chemical checks, foam control in washers and works re-wash eggs back into egg flow.
    • Grades eggs from the washers per SOP.
    • Provides for smooth transition of eggs from transfer room to breaking machine.
    • Keeps area clean.
    • Assists as needed during breaks and clean up.
    • Grades broken eggs from the breaking machine removing bad or blood spot eggs and shells from cups.
    • Performs clean up duties meeting USDA standards in Breaking, Transfer, and Shell rooms after production shift has ended.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Experience in Food Manufacturing or Processing desirable.
  • Safety programs and processes, such as Confined Space, LOTO, Hazcom, etc.
  • Equipment operation

Physical Demands

Stand and walk constantly; grip, grasp, push, pull, reach, bend, stoop, lift up to 10 pounds frequently; sit, climb, lift up to 50 pounds occasionally.

Work Environment

Frequently exposed to moving mechanical parts and water, and chemicals. Temperature is regulated for operations standards. Cooler temperatures occur in specific areas. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Proper personal protective equipment will be required during certain working conditions. Employees are required to comply with Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP’s) due to working in a food manufacturing environment (hairnets, clean clothes, etc.).

title: Sr Content Delivery Manager , Amazon MGM Studios
description:
We are looking for a Senior Content Delivery Manager based in Tokyo to lead content delivery and launch operations for Amazon MGM Studios growing Japan Originals slate. This role will serve as the strategic operational leader for Studio Content Services (SCS) in Japan, partnering closely with local Post Production and Production teams, the Global Delivery Manager, and teams across Studio Content Services, supporting both original productions and acquisitions for Amazon MGM Studios.

The Sr. Content Delivery Manager will lead the end-to-end Studio Content Services operational framework for Japan — designing and optimizing processes for intake, launch, and asset management while ensuring that each title (Movies and Series) receives successful: a) definition of deliverables, b) appropriate quality assurance for Original Version deliverables, c) timely intake of needed materials into Studio systems and processes, d) clean support for all streaming launch activities, and e) appropriate asset storage and management for downstream usage. The Sr. Content Delivery Manager will serve as the primary Studio Content Services point of contact for assigned titles, overseeing delivery schedules, solving complex challenges with internal stakeholders and external vendors, and ensuring content is delivered on time, on budget, and to the highest quality standards.

This role will lead the coordination of intake and launch operational support between the Japan-based operation and Amazon’s LA-based Global SCS teams, ensuring that local Japanese needs and time-zone requirements are addressed even while aspects of operations are handled elsewhere. The role requires building and implementing Studio Content Services operational strategies for the Japan territory — making trade-offs between short- and long-term needs, mitigating risk, and balancing speed, quality, and resource constraints as the Originals slate scales significantly.

This position is responsible for identifying and resolving complex operational challenges, making effective trade-offs between delivery timelines and studio release plans, and driving clear communication across languages, time zones, and organizational boundaries. The ideal candidate will be both tactical and strategic — comfortable managing multiple series and movies annually while simultaneously designing long-term solutions, scaling workflows, influencing partner teams to establish and grow Studio Content Services operations in Japan.

Key job responsibilities
1. Serve as the strategic Content Delivery leader for Japan, partnering with Japan Post Production, Global Delivery Manager, Studio Content Services Prime Video Delivery Operations and senior leaders to drive cross-functional initiatives and influence long-term operational goals, and author strategic documents (eg delivery SOPs, process improvements, slate status reports) to drive alignment.
2. Own and drive the on-time, on-budget delivery of movies and series produced and acquired in Japan, including partnering with Post on delivery budgets, ensuring all required assets are complete and delivered according to schedule.
3. Lead negotiations on delivery schedules with outside studios, producers, and production companies to meet overall release goals, make independent decisions on lower risk trade-offs and escalate high impact decisions as appropriate.
4. Actively manage intake processes for assigned titles, assess complex issues, mitigate risk, and drive resolution — serving as an escalation point for operational challenges across the Japan content pipeline.
5. Establish and maintain regular operational connection points between the Japan-based team and Global Studio Content Services in LA — including recurring status reporting, cross-timezone syncs, and intake/launch readiness checkpoints — to ensure continuous alignment and visibility across teams.
6. Drive best practices with external vendor relationships to deliver content on time and within budget, providing strategic guidance on technical requirements, QC processes, and operational expectations.
7. Identify, assess, and resolve technical or operational risks to delivery timelines that might impact studio release plans — proactively mitigating long-term risk rather than only escalating.
8. Design, implement, and continuously improve delivery guidelines and operational procedures, driving consistency and operational excellence across the Japan content pipeline and influencing standards globally.
9. Navigate organizational and process ambiguity in a fast-evolving environment, building operational strategies within a business-strategy context and adapting to shifting priorities, new workflows, and evolving team structures as the Japan Originals slate scales.
10. Advocate for and influence Japan-specific operational needs within the broader Global Studio Content Services framework, building strategic relationships with key stakeholders, and shaping processes and priorities to ensure effective local delivery.
11. Serve as the gatekeeper for sensitive communications between internal and external partners, exercising judgment on when to elevate information and when to limit communications to protect operational and business interests.


A day in the life
No two days look the same — and that’s by design. You’ll start your day syncing with the Global Studio Content Services team in LA before they sign off, and then shift focus to Japan-based partners across Post Production, production companies, and local vendors. A typical day includes managing active title pipelines, reviewing QC results, troubleshooting delivery blockers before launch windows, negotiating schedules with external studios, and driving intake / launch readiness. Cross-timezone syncs with Global Studio Content Services are a regular part of the rhythm – you'll bridge time zones and languages daily, ensuring nothing falls through the cracks between Tokyo and Los Angeles.

As the first hire in Japan, much of this role involves building — defining cadences, shaping workflows, and establishing the operational rhythm to meet launch expectations that will scale as the Japan Originals slate grows. You'll balance hands-on title management with the strategic work of building local Studio Content Services capabilities — addressing on-the-ground challenges, navigating local language dynamics with production teams and vendors, and providing dedicated in-market expertise that strengthens how Studio Content Services operates across the Japan slate.

About the team
Studio Content Services (SCS) owns all intake, management, and distribution operations for Amazon MGM Studios Originals globally — from defining deliverables with Post Production teams, to launching content on Prime Video, to managing assets through their full lifecycle including downstream licensing and preservation. We're a global team spanning LA, Singapore, and now Japan, operating at the intersection of creative and operations. Our culture values ownership, high standards, and trust — we move fast, solve hard problems collaboratively, and take pride in ensuring every title reaches customers at the highest quality.

This is the first dedicated hire in Japan, sitting at the intersection of Delivery, Localization, Content Operations, and PV Delivery Operations (PVDO) to serve as the local point of contact for all Studio Content Services functions. The role reports into the Global Delivery Manager in Singapore and partners closely with Global Studio Content Services in Los Angeles, bridging local production needs with Amazon's worldwide content operations. You'll be joining a team that's scaling rapidly to support a growing Japan Originals slate.

title: Software Engineer, SystemML - AI Networking
description:
In this role, you will be a member of the AI Networking Software team and part of the bigger DC networking organization. The team develops and owns the software stack around NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library), which enables multi-GPU and multi-node data communication through HPC-style collectives. NCCL has been integrated into PyTorch and is on the critical path of multi-GPU distributed training. In other words, nearly every distributed GPU-based ML workload in Meta Production goes through the software stack the team owns.

At the high level, the team aims to enable Meta-wide ML products and innovations to leverage our large-scale GPU training and inference fleet through an observable, reliable and high-performance distributed AI/GPU communication stack. Currently, one of the team’s focus is on building customized features, software benchmarks, performance tuners and software stacks around NCCL and PyTorch to improve the full-stack distributed ML reliability and performance (e.g. Large-Scale GenAI/LLM training) from the trainer down to the inter-GPU and network communication layer. And we are seeking engineers to work on the space of GenAI/LLM scaling reliability and performance.

  • Familiarity with software development life cycle (SDLC) and QA processes.

  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.

title: Idérig journalist søges til Bornholms Tidende
description:
På Bornholms Tidende laver vi uafhængig lokaljournalistik, der tager bornholmerne alvorligt, rejser debatten og dækker livet på øen. Skal du være med på holdet?

Bornholms Tidende søger en journalist, der både kan stå på egne ben og løfte i flok. Vi leder efter dig, der er idérig, tager ansvar, har næse for den gode historie og forstår værdien af et stærkt sammenhold på en redaktion med et fælles mål.


Du får mulighed for at præge dit eget stofområde. Det kan være et geografisk område, trafik, samfund eller noget helt fjerde, som du brænder særligt for og kan overbevise os om, at vi skal dække tæt. Vores hovedfokus er at skabe læsetid hos vores abonnenter, så din vigtigste kompetence er evnen til at skrive historier, som læserne har lyst til at bruge tid på.

Vi er drevet af lysten til at give vores abonnenter noget for pengene.
Vi har fokus på vores egen unikke journalistik, der er uafhængig af den generelle nyhedsdagsorden.

Hvem er du?

* Du er drevet af at lave god, gennemarbejdet journalistik baseret på egne og fælles ideer.
* Du er en holdspiller, der gerne deler viden, sparrer og bidrager til samarbejdet.
* Du leverer præcist og med kvalitet – også når det skal gå hurtigt.
* Du er klar til at engagere dig i Bornholm og livet herovre.

Hvem er vi?
Vi er optaget af at præge dagsordenen og fortælle historier, der både rammer dybt og bredt. Vi er et mediehus med over 160 års historie og stærke rødder i
lokalsamfundet – og en redaktion med frie rammer og godt humør. Hos os er der kort vej fra idé til publicering, og dine historier bliver læst og diskuteret i lokalsamfundet.

Skal du være med?
Har du lyst til at blive en del af holdet, og tror du på værdien af stærk lokaljournalistik?
Så send din ansøgning med cv til jdm@tidende.dk inden den 10. september klokken 12.00.

Du er også velkommen til at ringe til konstitueret chefredaktør Jesper Merved på 21625079, hvis du vil høre mere om stillingen, og hvad vi kan tilbyde.
Vi holder ansættelsessamtaler løbende og går efter tiltrædelse hurtigst muligt.

title: Senior Subcontracts Administrator
description:
Job Summary

The Senior Subcontracts Administrator builds, standardizes, and scales the subcontracting function supporting all CBRE Government Services portfolios. This is a full-time, salaried, project-funded role through March 31, 2027, with the potential to extend beyond that date. Reporting to the Sr. Manager of Subcontracts & Procurement, the position partners with Operations to implement consistent subcontracting processes, administer a portfolio of subcontracts, and ensure compliance with government contracting requirements and internal policies and procedures. The role requires deep FAR/DFARS knowledge, strong subcontract administration experience, structured change-management capability, and a proactive, solution-oriented approach. As the first point of escalation, the position provides decisive guidance to subcontract administration staff and helps resolve issues quickly and effectively.

Start date: October 1, 2026, or earlier as available

Primary Job Functions

  • Lead change management initiatives to implement a consistent subcontracting model across multiple business lines.
  • Partner with Operations leaders to define roles and responsibilities: Operations owns requirements, scopes, and budgets; Supply Chain leads solicitation strategy, competitive evaluation, award recommendations, and subcontract file compliance.
  • Facilitate workshops and process-mapping sessions to clarify handoffs throughout the subcontract lifecycle.
  • Drive adoption of standardized intake processes, documentation requirements, approval gates, and service expectations.
  • Collaborate with Operations on award recommendations so technical, commercial, and compliance factors are fully considered.
  • Establish communication routines and partnership structures supporting performance monitoring, corrective actions, change management, and closeout.
  • Manage the full lifecycle for assigned key subcontracts, including solicitation, negotiation, award, administration, and closeout.
  • Pre-award/Solicitation: Partner with Operations to understand requirements, strengthen procurement-type justifications, and prequalify suppliers as appropriate.
  • Negotiation: Confirm requirements are met and achieve best value or lowest price technically acceptable (LPTA).
  • Award: Follow required procedures to oblige funding and execute subcontracts and system purchase orders.
  • Administration: Support dispute resolution, invoice clarifications, subcontractor performance management, changes, and closeout.
  • Serve as a subject-matter expert on FAR, DFARS, the Service Contract Act, Davis-Bacon Act, collective bargaining agreements (SCA/DBA/CBA), other federal regulations, and company policies.
  • Coordinate with Finance, Legal, Compliance, and Supply Chain to align subcontractor deliverables with program milestones, support seamless execution, and resolve performance issues.
  • Mentor junior subcontract administrators and cross-functional business partners; provide subcontract administration guidance to mentor/protege small businesses as needed.
  • Apply a continuous-improvement mindset to challenge the status quo, conserve resources, and enable greater focus on strategic initiatives.

title: Fractional People & HR Consultant: USA - West Coast
description:
Independent Consultancy | Project-Based | Remote/Hybrid | Occasional Client Travel

Fractional People & HR Consultant — US West Coast
Location: San Francisco, San Francisco/Bay Area

PLEASE READ IN FULL BEFORE APPLYING

This is not a permanent employed position, and there is no guaranteed minimum number of hours.

If you're looking for:

  • A permanent HR position
  • Employee benefits
  • Guaranteed weekly hours
  • Visa sponsorship

Please do not apply.

This opportunity is for experienced People and HR professionals who enjoy variety, take ownership and want to join a growing consultancy supporting ambitious organisations across the US and internationally.

About Rosie's People

Rosie's People is an award-winning HR/People Operations and organisational consultancy supporting founders, leadership teams and growing organisations across the UK and internationally.

We provide strategic People advisory, organisational consulting, operational HR support, leadership and management development, talent solutions and executive recruitment.

As our international client portfolio continues to grow, we are expanding our network of experienced independent HR and People consultants across the United States.

We are particularly interested in consultants who can support clients in and around New York City, Washington DC and San Francisco, although applications from experienced consultants elsewhere in the US are also welcome.

HOW TO APPLY

Please submit your resume/CV together with a cover letter explaining why you believe you would be a strong addition to the Rosie's People consultant network.

Within your cover letter, please answer the following six mandatory questions.

Applications that do not answer all six questions will not be considered.

1. Location, Right to Work & Travel
Where are you currently based? Please confirm that you have the legal right to work as an independent consultant in the United States without sponsorship, and state which US cities/states you could reasonably support in person.

2. HR Experience & Employment Practice
How many years of substantive HR/People experience do you have? Please list the US states in which you have practical HR/employment experience and briefly describe one complex employee relations or People matter that you personally managed and the outcome.

3. Qualifications & Specialist Experience
Please list your relevant HR/People qualifications or certifications, including SHRM, HRCI or equivalent where applicable. Please also identify any specialist experience you have, for example organisational design, M&A/integration, restructuring, performance management, HR compliance, international HR, culture or leadership development.

4. Consultancy & International Working
Please briefly describe your experience working independently with senior stakeholders and/or clients. Include any experience supporting international, geographically distributed or cross-cultural teams and how you manage communication, ownership and escalation when operating as part of a wider consultancy or client team.

5. Availability & Consultancy Rates
What capacity could you typically make available for project work, and how quickly could you mobilise if selected for an assignment? Please provide your expected hourly and full-day consultancy rates in USD, excluding applicable taxes.

Applications stating market rate, negotiable, dependent on scope, or asking what the budget is or similar responses will not be considered.

6. AI, HR Systems & Technology
Please list the AI tools, HR systems and productivity software you have used professionally. Next to each, rate your competency as:

Beginner | Intermediate | Expert | Never Used

About the Opportunity

Successful applicants may be added to Rosie's People's approved consultant network and considered for client assignments as requirements arise.

Assignments may include:

  • Day-to-day and strategic HR support
  • Employee relations and manager advisory
  • Performance management
  • HR policies, processes and compliance
  • Organisational design and change
  • M&A and post-acquisition integration
  • Workforce planning and restructuring
  • Recruitment, onboarding and offboarding
  • HR audits and People-practice reviews
  • Supporting international and distributed workforces
  • Manager capability and organisational-development projects

Whilst you will manage your day-to-day workload independently, assignments will form part of Rosie's People's managed consultancy service and operate within agreed client scope, reporting, escalation and quality standards.

Our Ideal Consultant

We're looking for people who:

  • Have at least five years' substantive HR/People experience
  • Have strong practical knowledge of employment requirements applicable to the jurisdictions they support
  • Can confidently manage employee relations matters
  • Communicate credibly with managers, executives and founders
  • Are commercially minded, pragmatic and solutions-focused
  • Can enter a client environment and add value quickly
  • Understand the difference between independence and disappearing
  • Know when to take ownership, collaborate and escalate
  • Are comfortable with modern HR systems, AI tools and collaborative technology
  • Can represent the Rosie's People brand professionally

Relevant SHRM, HRCI or equivalent professional qualifications are desirable, although substantial practical experience will also be considered.

Important

Joining the Rosie's People consultant network does not constitute an offer or guarantee of work.

Client assignments are offered according to business requirements, expertise, location, availability, cultural/client fit and agreed commercial terms.

Where you are considered for a specific assignment, the scope, expected hours or days, duration, rate, travel requirements and other relevant terms will be agreed before any work commences.

Rosie's People is a remote-first, inclusive and equal opportunities consultancy. If you require reasonable adjustments during our selection process, please include a Reasonable Adjustment Request section within your cover letter.

title: Account / Project Coordinator
description:

We are seeking forward thinking candidates that have strong experience in operational support and can help take to the next level in a pro-active stance.

Chameleon Integrated Services has expertise in operations management, quality systems, data operations and cybersecurity. We secure some of the most sensitive data for the Department of Defense and for other U. S. federal government agencies. We are known for the great care we take with clients and employees, and we believe in promoting from within.

We offer a Full Benefits package including:

  • 100% company paid vision plan
  • 401K plan with generous company match and no vesting period
  • 100% company paid Life insurance
  • 100% company paid long and short-term disability insurance
  • Training allowance
  • PTO and more
Account / Project Coordinator

Work Location – Remote, (DHS treats remote network access as a privilege rather than a contractual guarantee, allowing work at assigned or other designated locations).
Security Clearance – U.S. Citizenship Required; Ability to complete DHS suitability, background investigation, and Entry-on-Duty requirements.
Experience – 3–5+ Years of Federal Project Coordination, PMO, Analytics-Program, or similar experience.
Length – 1-year intervals, up to 3 years.

Objective Summary
We are seeking an enterprise Account / Project Coordinator to provide vital operational support to the Engagement Manager and Program Manager. This critical position holds direct accountability for day-to-day schedule updates, meeting coordination, status tracking, and deliverable control across the OHSS Statement of Work. The ideal candidate must possess an extensive professional chronology demonstrating roughly 3–5+ years of continuous federal management support experience. This timeline should showcase strong proficiency maintaining action-item logs, calendar frameworks, and data-call documentation inside highly secured federal parameters.
This expert will maintain a rigorous document-quality discipline to keep cross-task technical teams organized while delivering recurring production tracking, calendar alignment, and project management office (PMO) support.

Mandatory Compliance Metrics
Candidates must satisfy these strict gates to ensure a successful Government onboarding determination:
  • Resume must explicitly reflect 3–5+ years of total federal project coordination or PMO experience validating support of technical analytics or professional services teams.
  • Must be fully available to attend and coordinate Government meetings between the hours of 8:30 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. Eastern, Monday through Friday.
  • Must accept a flexible management support posture capable of handling rapid document-control requests to maintain operational continuity without creating single-person failure points.
Principal Responsibilities
  • Provide high-level operational support directly to the Engagement Manager and Program Manager across all program schedules, meetings, and status reporting pipelines.
  • Establish and continuously maintain complete accountability over the program’s central action-item logs and deliverable tracking metrics.
  • Manage calendar architectures and cross-organizational schedule maintenance to ensure technical milestones stay aligned with federal deadlines.
  • Develop, monitor, and update the program's RAID (Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies) logs to escalate critical program blocks early.
  • Collect, format, and organize recurring status-report inputs from multidisciplinary technical teams to feed final executive updates.
  • Enforce absolute document control and a strict proofreading discipline to guarantee zero-defect text packages and report outputs for senior leadership.
  • Act as the logistical lead for data-call coordination, gathering required reference numbers and team inputs during sudden or unexpected Government requests.
  • Oversee and optimize everyday group collaboration tools leveraging Microsoft Office, Teams, SharePoint, or equivalent collaboration platforms.
Core Data & Architecture Capabilities
  • Expert level knowledge of federal PMO coordination frameworks including action-item registries, document configuration, and meeting log controls.
  • Familiarity with data analytics project environments, BI reporting workflows, and spreadsheet-driven tracking logic.
  • Functional understanding of federal reporting schedules supporting automated dashboards, data validation checks, and public website deployment cycles.
  • Experience working alongside contract delivery leads who administer blended Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Labor Hour task order elements.
Governance, Clearance & Government Infrastructure
  • Comprehensive mastery in safeguarding unclassified but sensitive government information, record-management data assets, and critical PII/SPII protection guidelines.
  • Direct experience operating inside federal civilian contracting parameters, GSA MAS task orders, and FAR-based compliance environments.
  • Familiarity with federal agency security awareness protocols, information system access requirements, and standard data-integrity tracking parameters.
Preferred Domain Expertise
  • Direct experience supporting data-intensive project management offices or analytics programs for DHS, CBP, ICE, USCIS, Census, DOJ, or HHS.
  • Deep functional understanding of homeland security mission settings, border statistics data flows, or law-enforcement program structures.
  • Active Project Management Institute credentials or certifications (such as CAPM or equivalent PMO tracking training).
  • Prior professional responsibility handling tracking and document control metrics for technical teams exceeding 10 individuals.

title: Systems Analyst
description:

If so, do we have the job for you!

*Ideal candidate will have experience with PointClickCare (PCC) or other electronic health record (EHR) system.*

Full-time, On-call Rotation

JOB SUMMARY

Configures, designs and maintains new and existing software systems. Works extensively with users to ensure the design of the software application supports the business requirements. Supportive of the Village’s mission, values, and service/hospitality (PRIDE) expectations. Completes training as required by policy.

ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

System Analysis and Design

  • Apply analysis techniques to both internal and third-party software systems with the goal being to ensure that the design and functionality of the software satisfies the clinical and business requirements of each care setting.
  • Works with the users to determine what forms/assessments are required in enterprise applications and then builds the forms/assessments using internal application tools.
  • Work with key stakeholders to study their processes and identify where new processes or process modifications are required. Subsequently modifies the design and configuration of the software — designing and building new processes, creating/revising forms and assessments, redesigning security infrastructure and configuring these elements in the software, updating required field status on fields available to the users and other system design/configuration updates as required.
  • Work with users to determine appropriate and effective hardware and software tools required for the business need.
  • Work extensively with the users to analyze software problems and develop appropriate solutions.
  • Train users on software functionality.
  • Use creative skills to quickly resolve the most critical problems that occur in production applications, systems software and their supporting environments.

Database Application Support

  • After identifying a new system requirement, design the system workflow that will support the business need and then work with the senior systems analyst to develop/redesign the added/enhanced functionality. Subsequently, test the new/enhanced functionality for flaws or required redesign.
  • Test and apply software updates.
  • Design reports.
  • Maintain expertise in current application software and hardware technologies.
  • Provide after-hours support for on-call and regular maintenance for software applications.

Electronic Health Record System Analysis

  • Consult with users to identify needs and develop efficient workflow processes for all software that addresses electronic health record capture and storage.
  • Evaluate and recommend computer systems, if required.
  • Research commercially available software to meet Village needs.
  • Adheres to all safety regulations and requirements.
  • Handles stress well and gets along with others within the workplace and with customers outside the department.
  • Maintains acceptable standards of workplace conduct.

The responsibilities described above represent the primary responsibilities of the job. Other responsibilities may be assigned by the supervisor as warranted by business needs. The incumbent is expected to perform all assigned responsibilities.

ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

  • This job requires a combination of education, training and/or experience that would typically be acquired through a course of study leading to Associate's degree (A. A.) or equivalent from two-year College or technical school, preferably in computer science.

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Must have a valid driver’s license. Must carry proof of auto insurance.

Knowledge and Skills (required unless otherwise noted):

  • Previous experience in healthcare or IT support preferred.
  • Advanced keyboarding skills.
  • Advanced skills using Microsoft Windows and Microsoft Office software (Excel, Word, Access and PowerPoint).
  • Intermediate level knowledge of Microsoft SQL is preferred.
  • Ability to read, analyze and interpret the most complex documents.
  • Ability to write reports, business correspondence, and procedure manuals.
  • Ability to speak effectively before groups of customers or associates of the organization.
  • Ability to calculate figures and amounts such as discounts, interest, commissions, proportions, percentages, area, circumference and volume.
  • Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions.
  • Ability to interpret and understand federal and state regulations.

description:

At Vista Pointe at Sierra Vista, we are dedicated to enriching the lives of our residents through compassionate care and unwavering support. Full-time benefits include:

  • PTO (Paid Time Off) and Holiday Pay: Take advantage of paid time off to maintain a healthy work-life balance.

  • Health/Dental Insurance
  • 401K with employer match: Plan for your financial future with our 401k program.

  • Referral Bonuses: Refer qualified candidates and earn rewards

Summary of Duties of the Medication Technician

The primary responsibilities of the Medication Technician are as follows: 1) Administer or assist with the administration and/or supervision of medications to the residents in a safe, accurate, and timely manner (dependent on State regulations); 2) Provide physical and psychosocial care to all residents in a manner that promotes dignity, choice, and individuality; and 3) Responsible for overseeing the wellness staffing schedule. The Medication Technician reports to the supervisor on duty as well as the Wellness Director.

Essential Functions of the Medication Technician

  • Administers or assists with or supervises the administration of medications according to the physician order on the medication administration record (MAR).
  • Documents medications administered on the MAR in accordance with company policy; Checks MARs immediately after administration and prior to end of shift to ensure documentation is complete and accurate.
  • Conducts change of shift report with oncoming/outgoing shift personnel.
  • Maintains security of medication cart and narcotic keys during entire shift; Conducts narcotic count at the beginning and end of every shift in accordance with company policies and procedures.
  • Provides assistance with activities of daily living such as with bathing, dressing, personal hygiene (includes shaving, oral care, nail care, hair care, foot care), toileting, eating, and ambulation/mobility.
  • Works collaboratively with peers and other team members.
  • Maintains professional demeanor at all times when interacting with residents and families.
  • Reports any suspected or witnessed instances of verbal, mental, or physical abuse to licensed staff immediately.
  • Utilizes safe transfer techniques when assisting residents with mobility.
  • Observes and reports changes in residents’ physical condition and cognitive/emotional status to Wellness Director or charge nurse, as needed.
  • Assists residents with swallowing difficulty with eating.
  • Responds to emergencies in a prompt and calm manner; Immediately reports such emergencies to the charge nurse and/or Wellness Director.
  • Understands and uses Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Standard Precautions, OSHA's Occupational Exposure to Bloodborne Pathogens standard, and follows established infection control procedures, hazardous communication, and other safety rules.
  • Ensures cleanliness of residents' rooms and promptly reports all violations of safety and sanitation rules to supervisor.
  • Documents provision of services on company forms.
  • Operates designated medical equipment, copy, scan, fax machines, and telephone.
  • Responsible for planning the wellness schedule preferably 1 month in advance but no less than 2 weeks.
  • Participates in an on-call rotation for staffing needs; Will be responsible for finding coverage for open shifts.
  • Must be available by phone 24/7 while on-call for staffing needs and able to fill open shift if needed.

Non-Essential Functions of the Medication Technician

  • Provides all necessary care and services to assigned residents and assists other wellness associates as needed.
  • Participates in and supports the resident-centered activities program.
  • Cares for sensory enhancement devices such as eyeglasses and hearing aids.
  • Completes housekeeping tasks such as bed-making, linen changes, vacuuming, emptying trash, and cleaning bathrooms.
  • Washes resident’s laundry as needed.
  • Escorts residents and coordinates internal transportation needs.
  • Assists residents with personal correspondence/telephone use when requested.
  • Conducts room checks and resident rounds.
  • Monitors for environmental safety hazards.
  • Assists in a variety of tasks related to dining (escort residents to dining room, assist with set-up and clean tables, serve meals, bus tables, etc.).
  • Attends and participates in staff meetings and mandatory in-services.
  • Uses tactful, diplomatic communication techniques in potentially sensitive or emotionally charged situations.
  • Follows-up with appropriate staff, residents, or other individuals regarding reported complaints, problems, and concerns.
  • Acts as an ambassador and public relations representative to guests and other visitors.
  • Demonstrates an appreciation of the heritage, values and wisdom of the residents, and an understanding of the aging process.
  • Collaborates with associates in other departments to assure necessary care and services are provided.
  • Participates in projects or committees as assigned.
  • Performs related duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Experience

  • Must maintain certification in the state where you work if required.
  • Satisfactory completion of state-required education/certificates/testing in relation to medication aides as well as the company medication aide skills competency checklist.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak in English.
  • Be in good physical health and free of communicable diseases; Lifting, bending, and pushing medication cart about residence is required; Must be able to lift 40 pounds.
  • Completion of drug testing and criminal background check upon hire and upon request of supervisor.
  • Experience in Assisted Living preferred.

title: Project Services Consultant or Senior Consultant
description:
Overview

MPR is seeking an experienced Project Services Consultant (or Project Services Senior Consultant) to play a lead role in our risk-informed approach to development, planning, and execution of complex commercial and government capital projects in nuclear, fossil, and renewable power generation, nuclear materials processing, power transmission, energy storage and distribution, and radioactive waste processing and storage/disposition. The ideal candidate will possess broad consulting competencies, engineering and regulatory experience, and deep domain knowledge of project controls to lead our multi-disciplinary project teams in delivery of high-value integrated technical and project solutions tailored to the unique needs of our client’s strategic, complex, and technically challenging projects.

MPR's Project Services Consultants deliver comprehensive project management, project controls and cost engineering capabilities across the full project lifecycle. Our services include program planning and strategy development, organizational planning, critical path methodology (CPM) scheduling, cost estimating and control, earned value management (EVM), risk management program development, qualitative and quantitative risk analysis, project performance measurement and reporting, project controls procedure development, and constructability assessments.

What sets MPR apart is our deep technical understanding of our clients' industries and challenges, enabling high-value solutions that proactively identify and mitigate project risks. We work flexibly across diverse roles, including, but not limited to: serving in EPC project controls leadership positions, providing construction management and oversight for nuclear, fossil, and renewable power projects, implementing PMO startup services for utilities and technology providers, and performing independent cost/schedule/risk reviews for project owners. Our broad experience with all major industry players, from architect/engineers and nuclear technology vendors to OEMs, fabricators, and constructors, enables us to deliver tailored solutions that meet the needs of all stakeholders, from work package managers to C-suite executives.

Duties/Responsibilities

The Project Services Consultant (or Project Services Senior Consultant) will:

  • Deliver PMO support, program development, and independent project reviews for clients across MPR’s federal, power, and energy business sectors (including DOE, DoD, DHS programs, new nuclear reactor vendors and project developers, power utilities, and energy storage developers).
  • Lead multi-disciplinary project teams in early-stage program development, including program justification and approval support, alternatives analysis, technology readiness assessments, preliminary cost/schedule/risk evaluations, regulatory guidance, and baseline development.
  • Implement project controls systems, optimize delivery schedules and critical path recovery, develop EVM systems and performance metrics, and perform cost/benefit evaluations to improve client project execution.
  • Plan, lead, and provide subject matter expertise for independent project reviews of large-scale capital projects, including independent cost estimating, schedule assessments, quantitative risk analysis, EVM assessments, technology maturity reviews, and constructability evaluations.
  • Engage directly with clients, contractors, and stakeholders to communicate findings and recommendations, ensuring solutions address project challenges and decision-maker needs while serving as a steward of client resources with transparent, independent feedback.
  • Plan, lead, and enable multi-disciplinary project teams to support our Project Services work, including coaching and mentoring other professionals through execution of the work.
  • Review work and analyses performed by other MPR professionals.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Finance, Business Administration or other technical disciplines is a strong plus. Candidates without a bachelor's degree will be considered based on commensurate experience.
  • Certifications from AACE International (Association for the Advancement of Cost Engineering) are a plus but not required: Certified Cost Professional (CCP), Certified Estimating Professional (CEP), Earned Value Professional (EVP), Decision and Risk Management Professional (DRMP).

Technical Experience

  • 5+ years work experience (10+ years for the Senior Consultant position) as a project management/project controls professional working in the power/energy industry and/or for large government programs/capital acquisition projects.
  • Experience in multiple disciplines of project management/project controls consulting and cost engineering. NOTE: Candidates will be evaluated on breadth (exposure to multiple disciplines) and depth (expertise in selected disciplines).
    • Project Planning and CPM Scheduling- Experience developing and maintaining GAO compliant Work Breakdown Structures and Integrated Master Schedules (baseline and forecast) in Oracle Primavera P6, implementing resource dictionaries, conducting schedule-based resource analysis and resource leveling, and developing summary level schedules with vertical traceability to detailed working schedules
    • Cost Estimating- Experience developing cost estimates across all phases of project maturity, from conceptual parametric estimates to detailed bottom-up estimates, including uncertainty analysis, and the application of AACE Recommended Practices and GAO best practices
    • Cost Control and EVM- Experience implementing, maintaining, and applying Earned Value Management Systems (EVMS) on large capital projects in accordance with industry standards (e.g., ANSI/EIA-748 or equivalent client governance requirements) to support integrated planning, budgeting, performance measurement, variance analysis, forecasting, and management reporting
    • Risk Management and Quantitative Risk Analysis- Experience developing and implementing risk management programs consistent with DOE O 413.3B or DoD Risk Management Guide for Defense Acquisition Programs DoDI 5000.90 to include RMPs, risk registers, qualitative analysis guidelines, heat mapping action tracking- Experience with quantitative cost and schedule risk analysis using Monte Carlo simulation techniques, including integrated cost/schedule risk analysis, to develop program/project contingency budgets and to identify key risk drivers and risk-informed critical paths
    • Enterprise Resource Planning- Experience implementing, integrating, and administering ERP systems that support WBS-based budgeting, project accounting, procurement, inventory management, workflow automation, financial reporting, and seamless integration with project controls and earned value management systems
    • Project Lifecycle Management- Experience planning and managing capital projects through all phases of the project lifecycle under DOE O 413.3B, DoD acquisition, utility stage-gate, and other capital project governance frameworks, including project execution planning, estimate maturation, contingency and management reserve planning, baseline evolution, and project phase transitions

title: Medication Technician
location: Lake Havasu City, Arizona, United States
description:
At Vista Pointe at Lake Havasu City, we are dedicated to enriching the lives of our residents through compassionate care and unwavering support. We are seeking individuals who share our commitment to creating exceptional living experiences and who are eager to contribute to a supportive, family-like atmosphere. When you join Vista Pointe at Lake Havasu City, you become an integral part of a team that values making a positive difference every single day. If you are driven by empathy and excellence, we invite you to bring your talents to our welcoming community.

Full-time benefits include:

  • PTO (Paid Time Off) and Holiday Pay: Take advantage of paid time off to maintain a healthy work-life balance.
  • Daily pay: Get paid daily, providing you with financial flexibility and control over your earnings.
  • Health/Dental Insurance
  • 401K with employer match: Plan for your financial future with our 401k program.
  • Life Insurance: Company paid life insurance
  • Short and long-term disability: Financial security while you recover from an injury that puts you out of work
  • Referral Bonuses: Refer qualified candidates and earn rewards
  • Tuition Reimbursement: Invest in your education with our support
  • Employee Assistance Program: Connecting our employees with resources for handling personal challenges

Summary of Duties of the Medication Technician

The primary responsibilities of the Medication Technician are as follows: 1) Administer or assist with the administration and/or supervision of medications to the residents in a safe, accurate, and timely manner (dependent on State regulations); 2) Provide physical and psychosocial care to all residents in a manner that promotes dignity, choice, and individuality; and 3) Responsible for overseeing the wellness staffing schedule. The Medication Technician reports to the supervisor on duty as well as the Wellness Director.

Essential Functions of the Medication Technician

  • Administers or assists with or supervises the administration of medications according to the physician order on the medication administration record (MAR).
  • Documents medications administered on the MAR in accordance with company policy; Checks MARs immediately after administration and prior to end of shift to ensure documentation is complete and accurate.
  • Conducts change of shift report with oncoming/outgoing shift personnel.
  • Maintains security of medication cart and narcotic keys during entire shift; Conducts narcotic count at the beginning and end of every shift in accordance with company policies and procedures.
  • Provides assistance with activities of daily living such as with bathing, dressing, personal hygiene (includes shaving, oral care, nail care, hair care, foot care), toileting, eating, and ambulation/mobility.
  • Works collaboratively with peers and other team members.
  • Maintains professional demeanor at all times when interacting with residents and families.
  • Reports any suspected or witnessed instances of verbal, mental, or physical abuse to licensed staff immediately.
  • Utilizes safe transfer techniques when assisting residents with mobility.
  • Observes and reports changes in residents’ physical condition and cognitive/emotional status to Wellness Director or charge nurse, as needed.
  • Assists residents with swallowing difficulty with eating.
  • Responds to emergencies in a prompt and calm manner; Immediately reports such emergencies to the charge nurse and/or Wellness Director.
  • Understands and uses Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Standard Precautions, OSHA's Occupational Exposure to Bloodborne Pathogens standard, and follows established infection control procedures, hazardous communication, and other safety rules.
  • Ensures cleanliness of residents' rooms and promptly reports all violations of safety and sanitation rules to supervisor.
  • Documents provision of services on company forms.
  • Operates designated medical equipment, copy, scan, fax machines, and telephone.
  • Responsible for planning the wellness schedule preferably 1 month in advance but no less than 2 weeks.
  • Participates in an on-call rotation for staffing needs; Will be responsible for finding coverage for open shifts.
  • Must be available by phone 24/7 while on-call for staffing needs and able to fill open shift if needed.

Non-Essential Functions of the Medication Technician

  • Provides all necessary care and services to assigned residents and assists other wellness associates as needed.
  • Participates in and supports the resident-centered activities program.
  • Cares for sensory enhancement devices such as eyeglasses and hearing aids.
  • Completes housekeeping tasks such as bed-making, linen changes, vacuuming, emptying trash, and cleaning bathrooms.
  • Washes resident’s laundry as needed.
  • Escorts residents and coordinates internal transportation needs.
  • Assists residents with personal correspondence/telephone use when requested.
  • Conducts room checks and resident rounds.
  • Monitors for environmental safety hazards.
  • Assists in a variety of tasks related to dining (escort residents to dining room, assist with set-up and clean tables, serve meals, bus tables, etc.).
  • Attends and participates in staff meetings and mandatory in-services.
  • Uses tactful, diplomatic communication techniques in potentially sensitive or emotionally charged situations.
  • Follows-up with appropriate staff, residents, or other individuals regarding reported complaints, problems, and concerns.
  • Acts as an ambassador and public relations representative to guests and other visitors.
  • Demonstrates an appreciation of the heritage, values and wisdom of the residents, and an understanding of the aging process.
  • Collaborates with associates in other departments to assure necessary care and services are provided.
  • Participates in projects or committees as assigned.
  • Performs related duties as assigned.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, and Experience

  • Must maintain certification in the state where you work if required.
  • Satisfactory completion of state-required education/certificates/testing in relation to medication aides as well as the company medication aide skills competency checklist.
  • Ability to read, write, and speak in English.
  • Be in good physical health and free of communicable diseases; Lifting, bending, and pushing medication cart about residence is required; Must be able to lift 40 pounds.
  • Completion of drug testing and criminal background check upon hire and upon request of supervisor.
  • Experience in Assisted Living preferred.

title: Mass Spectrometrist
description:
Working at Yale means contributing to a better tomorrow. Whether you are a current resident of our New Haven-based community, eligible for opportunities through the New Haven Hiring Initiative, or a newcomer, interested in exploring all that Yale has to offer, your talents and contributions are welcome. Discover your opportunities at Yale!

Overview

The Yale Chemical and Biophysical Instrumentation Center (CBIC) is a broad collection of scientific instruments for chemistry and biochemistry research, including mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and X-ray crystallography, all overseen by a professional staff. This position is for a staff scientist specializing in mass spectrometry. Under the supervision of the CBIC Director, the staff scientist will manage technical and scientific tasks essential to the mass spectrometry facility’s operations and guide projects within the research core by managing experimental design and data analysis. The position will provide training and/or guidance to core users contributing to the development of experimental protocols.

CBIC staff scientists maintain and operate the center’s instruments and provide training and support to allow researchers to operate these instruments themselves, as appropriate. This position will provide user training and expert advice, service operation and custom analyses, as well as maintenance and oversight of CBIC mass spectrometers. The staff scientist will assist with new instrument acquisitions and upgrades and provide oversight and support for other instrumentation as needed. Additionally, the staff scientist will collaborate with university research teams and faculty members on research, grants, reports, presentations, and publications to support the CBIC’s training and research missions.


Required Skills and Abilities

1. Demonstrated broad knowledge and hands-on training in the theory and practice of mass spectrometry, including practical experience operating, maintaining and/or repairing mass spectrometers

2. Strong communication skills and ability to effectively train users and staff on proper procedures and methods for using mass spectrometers as well as processing and interpreting mass spectrometry data.

3. Demonstrated skill and understanding of state-of-art mass spectrometry including the ability to provide technical support for collaborative design and execution of modern mass spectrometry methods.

4. Ability to repair, maintain and modify scientific instruments. Computer skills for instrument operation and data analysis.


Preferred Skills and Abilities

1. PhD in Chemistry or related field

2. Good interpersonal and communication skills to facilitate working with faculty and students to assist them in operating instruments and interpreting data.

3. Knowledge and ability to work with other instrumentation such as solution biophysics and/or optical spectroscopy, including operating and maintaining these instruments and associated computers and software.

Principal Responsibilities

1. User Training: Provide advanced training and guidance to users of the research core. 2. Experiment Support: Collaborate with researchers on experimental design, execution, data analysis, and troubleshooting within the research core. 3. Facility/Instrument Support: Manage and oversee research projects within the research core. 4. Technique Development: Lead the implementation and optimization of advanced techniques and methodologies and develop standard operating procedures for research core services. 5. Data Analysis/Interpretation: Analyze and interpret complex scientific data, generating meaningful insights and recommendations. 6. Equipment Procurement: Assist in the selection, acquisition, and maintenance of research core equipment. 7. Professional Development: Stay updated with emerging research trends and technologies. Participate in professional development activities and scientific conferences. 8. Scientific Participation: Contribute scientific data for manuscript preparation and grant proposals 9. Staff Training and Mentoring: Contribute to the training and mentoring of junior staff members. 10. Vendor Relations: Manage vendor relationships, negotiates contracts, and evaluates new technologies for optimal procurement processes. 11. Education and Outreach: Contribute to education and outreach activities within the core, including tours, events, etc. Required Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree in a related discipline and four years of related experience or an equivalent combination of skills, education, and experience.

All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of the background check. For additional information on the background check requirements and process visit "Learn about background checks" under the Applicant Support Resources section of Careers on the It's Your Yale website.

title: Bilingual Conservation Learning Specialist - Child & Family Discovery
description:
Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance (DZCA) honors our animals, staff, and guests by conducting ourselves at the highest level of integrity through our Core Actions -- Inspire Awe: Safety, Care, Connect and by embracing our Core Values of: Welcoming, Curious, United, Courageous, and Transformative in all that we do.

The Bilingual Conservation Learning Specialist: Child and Family Discovery serves as a staff member at will of Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance (DZCA). In that capacity, this position will advance the mission of DZCA through the facilitation and support of programs that build foundational connections to nature for young children and their caregivers, developing interest and affinity for wildlife and the natural world, and strengthening their ability to engage in developmentally appropriate conservation action.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Program Facilitation

  • Facilitate science and conservation learning through dynamic implementation of pre-written programs, including:
    • Nature play opportunities and programs for young children (ages 2-5) and their families.
    • Learning experiences for K-12 students during school field trips or through community outreach.
    • Day camp programs, including instruction and operational support.
  • Apply best practices in conservation education facilitation; adapt curricula and program plans to changing circumstances; flex facilitation style to best meet the needs of participants.
  • Handle live animals and biofacts; use and problem-solve technology, and drive DZCA vehicles (including the RV-based Neighborhood Nature Explorer) in support of programs.

Program Support and Development

  • Partner with Program Coordinators to execute program logistics: create, prepare, set up, break down, maintain, inventory, and clean program materials and supplies. Load and unload materials and supplies for community outreach programs.
  • As assigned, develop and update programs using the organizational program design process.
  • Collect, enter, and report program data, including attendance.
  • Model best practices for staff and volunteers and assist in the development or training of staff and volunteers as assigned.

Communication

  • Provide excellent program communication; communicate in clear language and adjust the use of language to participants’ level of understanding.
  • Communicate effectively and professionally with all DZCA staff members; proactively communicate with department and program leaders about program needs and concerns; regularly check and communicate about varied and changing schedules.
  • Demonstrates and advocates for a positive and inclusive team culture.

Self-Development

  • Actively seek feedback and professional development opportunities to strengthen program facilitation, curriculum development, proactive engagement, developmentally appropriate teaching, empathy-building, and conservation learning practices.

Other Duties/Responsibilities

  • Other assistance, as designated by the Conservation Learning Coordinators or Managers, to support the overall goals of the department and organization. DZCA retains the right to add or change duties and/or responsibilities at any time.
  • While this position does not include formal supervisory responsibilities, it plays a key role in modeling best practices and may provide training, mentorship, and support to seasonal and part-time educators, as well as volunteers, in alignment with program goals.
  • The nature of this position requires safeguarding against the release of confidential and proprietary information of DZCA.
  • This position will interact with staff members across the organization, volunteers, members of external organizations, and the public, and will represent DZCA professionally and positively.

Technical / Professional Requirements & Qualifications

  • Completion or in pursuit of a high school degree or equivalent required, or any equivalent combination of education and/or experience.
  • Requires a minimum of 1 year of experience in environmental education in a nonprofit zoo or museum of science institution.
  • Experience and comfort working with children of various ages and with diverse communities is strongly preferred, or any equivalent combination of experience, lived experience, and/or special skills.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Requires demonstrated knowledge and dynamic skills in program facilitation and informal learning strategies; comfort in nature; experience engaging children in natural spaces preferred. Preference is given to candidates who have done so successfully in an informal biological or conservation education setting.
  • Requires organizational skills, written and oral communication skills, attention to detail, and ability to prioritize work and tasks.
  • Requires adaptability to produce and meet deadlines in a fast-paced, multi-task, and changing environment, and the ability to work as part of a team.
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite.
  • Ability to communicate and facilitate programs in English and Spanish is preferred.
  • Requires the ability to drive outreach vehicles, including vans and a small Class C RV, after provided training.
  • Ability to communicate and facilitate programs in English and Spanish is strongly preferred, with a pay differential for verified fluency.

Position Conditions

  • Ability to pass a background check and pre-employment drug and alcohol screen.
  • To support our operational policies, candidates must be at least 21 years of age with a valid driver's license and a clean driving record.
  • Schedule Availability: The schedule follows a Tuesday – Saturday workweek, including weekends as regular workdays and occasional flexibility for seasonal operational or evening support.
  • Work Location: Primarily in-person, with programming delivered both on campus and at community locations.

Compensation

The range for this position is $20.85 - $24.50 (hourly).

For Bilingual: A pay differential will be paid for positions requiring Spanish speaking fluency.

A Truly Wild Workplace with Competitive Benefits

Join our team and enjoy a wide variety of great benefits, including:

  • Comprehensive medical, vision, and dental coverage
  • 403(b) Retirement Account with employer match
  • Generous paid time off: vacation, sick leave, personal days, and holidays
  • A Family DZCA Membership with discounted tickets to special events
  • Concession and retail discounts, plus free parking
  • And so much more!

We encourage all qualified candidates to apply. If you're passionate about contributing to a dynamic, mission-driven organization, we want to hear from you!

    Application Process and Timelines

    This position will remain open until filled. Applications will be reviewed as they are received, and interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis until operational needs are met. DZCA reserves the right to close the position at any time.

    Denver Zoo Conservation Alliance is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

description:
